nba_directive.reason_text: Client wants to delay, but with a 6.75% rate and $307K balance there is real, quantifiable savings potential on the table — pinning a concrete callback with break-even math tied to their stated goal prevents this lead from going cold.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by anchoring their exact current position
  - State their rate: 6.75% conventional, $2,092/mo P&I, $307,013 remaining
  - Ask or confirm their stated life goal (retirement timeline, debt freedom date, specific event) so the scenario is personal, not generic

- Quantify the gap before honoring the delay
  - Pull today's achievable rate for their profile and show the spread vs. 6.75%
  - Calculate the new estimated P&I at that rate on $307,013 and present the monthly delta in real dollars (do not guess — run the actual quote)
  - Multiply monthly savings × 12 to show the annual cost of waiting
  - Present break-even: closing costs ÷ monthly savings = months to recoup; if break-even is under their stated goal horizon, name that explicitly

- Counter the 'wait for rates to drop' instinct with reframe math
  - Show how many months of delay = one full break-even period lost
  - Remind them: if rates drop further after closing, they can refinance again — this is not a one-way door
  - Tie the cost of waiting back to their specific goal ('every month at 6.75% is $X that doesn't go toward [their goal]')

- Honor the delay but pin it to a hard date and time
  - Acknowledge their timeline without abandoning the conversation
  - Propose a specific callback: 'Can we lock in 10 minutes on [specific day/time] so I can walk you through the exact numbers?'
  - Confirm the callback in writing via text immediately after they agree

- Set a follow-up tripwire — do not go silent
  - If no response within 48 hours, send one short re-engagement text referencing the monthly savings figure computed above
  - Do not repeat a generic equity pitch — reference only the rate gap and their stated goal
